newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rupee ends up in kerb, seen firm.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed 0.05 up at 41.42 to the dollar on Tuesday amid low demand for the U.S. currency at the start of fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) and would remain firm in the near term, dealers said.
"The dollar demand was depressed owing to a liquidity crunch," dealer Owais Kalia said. "Many big investors are on summer holidays, which is a factor for the low dollar demand."

The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, fixed on June 28, was at 40.4600/40.6623 rupees to the dollar. The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates ended at 2.50 percent from 2.65 on Monday. -- Amir Zia 9221-5685192
